lead: Taylor's self-titled debut is turning 20, and her official site has given it a room of its own. Fans found the new archive section in late October, while the album's rerecorded version is still waiting on a release date.

sentences.text: Fans noticed a new "20 years of Taylor Swift" section on taylorswift.com on October 23, Yahoo says.
It gathers streaming links, photos, career highlights and the earliest music videos in one place.
Taylor Nation marked the anniversary with an Instagram clip that runs through every one of her eras.
Taylor herself stayed quiet on social media for the day.
Swifties will happily lose an afternoon in that archive.
In her letter about buying back her first six masters, Taylor said she had already rerecorded the whole debut album, Elle notes.
No release of that version has been announced.
The anniversary also brings back an early near miss: Richard Marx turned down a co-write with a 15-year-old Taylor after Scott Borchetta played him her first demos.
Two decades later, he still says he wouldn't have been any good to her.

lead: Taylor's three-week reign at the top of the Hot 100 is over, and the numbers behind the drop point to a quiet week for physical copies. "Patient Zero" now shares the top five with three brand-new debuts.

sentences.text: Taylor's "Patient Zero" slipped from No. 1 to No. 5 this week, ending her run at the top, Rolling Stone reports.
With no new variants or shipments to buy, physical sales fell from 151,000 to 26,000, Variety says.
The acoustic versions Taylor released still added 4,000 downloads to the week.
Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" is back at No. 1 for a 25th nonconsecutive week, with Tate McRae's "Housewife" debuting right behind it at No. 2 on 22.9 million streams.
For Taylor, the slide follows a historic start: the song debuted at No. 1 as her 16th chart-topper and her 10th to enter at the summit, tying Drake's record.
Across the Atlantic, it also spent three straight weeks at No. 1 in the UK while "The Life of a Showgirl" reached 15 weeks atop the Billboard 200.
Honestly, a slide like this after a run like that barely counts as a dip.

lead: The girl who signed a publishing deal at 14 is now in the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame. Taylor was inducted on Monday night as its youngest member ever, with Brad Paisley doing the honors at a gala in Nashville.

sentences.text: Brad Paisley inducted Taylor at the hall's gala at Music City Center on October 26, Rolling Stone reports.
She joined a class of six that also included Lyle Lovett and Lee Thomas Miller, with one inductee honored posthumously.
In her speech, she went back to the very beginning, recalling that she signed with Sony Publishing when she was 14.
Honestly, this is the most Taylor thing she's done all year.
Lainey Wilson marked the moment with a stripped-down acoustic "Love Story," Variety says.
George Strait was honored at the same ceremony too, collecting the Career Maker Award.
The gala made official a vote from August, when the hall named her a 2026 inductee and the youngest songwriter it has ever elected.
It is her second hall of fame induction of the year, the Associated Press notes, after she became the youngest woman ever inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame.

lead: A new report puts a dollar figure on a surprise performance Nelly joined Taylor for, and it matches a number Nelly has mentioned himself. Almost everything else about that night, from the venue to the date, is still missing from the story.

sentences.text: TMZ reports that Taylor paid Nelly $50,000 to join her for a surprise performance.
A News.com.au headline describes it as a three-minute gig.
Neither outlet names a venue or a city.
The report carries no comment from Taylor's team or from Nelly.

Fans already know a version of this story from Nelly himself: on The Breakfast Club and Good Day New York, he said Taylor called before two Houston shows to explain she was working with a limited budget.
By his telling, her manager, Robert Allen, then handed him the money in a McDonald's bag.
Ashanti joined him in those interviews, and the two described a friendship with Taylor that has now lasted for years.
Coverage of his account still disagrees on when the Houston shows happened.
Whatever the real date, that bag-of-cash detail is the kind of tour lore Swifties will happily repeat forever.

lead: The Bluebird Cafe has a gentle message for anyone planning a Nashville pilgrimage this week: its two-day closure has nothing to do with Taylor. A viral theory timed to her Hall of Fame moment ran into a far simpler explanation.

sentences.text: Taylor was set to join the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame on October 26.
A day earlier, a TikToker went viral suggesting she might make a surprise return to the Bluebird.
Fans then spotted a private-event closure on the venue's calendar for October 27 and 28, Country Living notes.
The Bluebird says the closures are for unrelated filming that happens to fall the same week.
It has asked fans not to show up while it is closed.
Cosmopolitan's verdict is that she will not be playing there this week.
The week still delivered its Nashville moment: Brad Paisley inducted her as the hall's youngest member ever, and she spent nearly 10 minutes on Music Row, Liz Rose and being 14.
Her last publicly reported Bluebird set was a surprise appearance in 2018.
